proposals.before: Su Chuo had been in office for more than a year before Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai truly knew his worth.
proposals.after: Su Chuo had been in office for more than a year, and Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai did not yet know him deeply.
proposals.reason: Chinese 未深知之 means Tai did not yet know him deeply; 'truly knew his worth' changes the sense.

proposals.before: As for transformation—it prizes being able to fan it with pure wind, steep it in the Great Harmony, cover it with morality and virtue, show it simplicity and plainness.
proposals.after: As for transformation—it prizes being able to fan it with pure wind, steep it with the Great Harmony, cover it with morality and virtue, show it simplicity and plainness.
proposals.reason: Source has corrupt 乙 for 以 in 浸之乙太和; literal should follow intended 浸之以太和 ('steep it with/by').
Chinese unit is only the corrupt fragment （五） from 三五以來; bracketed English invents a clause not in this unit.

proposals.before: since then, every age has had systems of taxation.
proposals.after: Since the Three and Five, every age has had systems of taxation.
proposals.reason: Chinese 三以來 is the broken remainder of classical 三五以來 after （五） was split off; 'since then' drops that chronology.

proposals.before: The Pillar of State and all the grandees and ranking generals came to court without exception.
proposals.after: Pillar-of-State Yuwen Tai and all the grandees and ranking generals came to court without exception.
proposals.reason: Chinese 柱國泰 names Yuwen Tai; the idiomatic English omits 泰.

proposals.before: The Pillar of State and all the grandees and ranking generals, none failed to come to court.
proposals.after: Pillar-of-State Tai and all the grandees and ranking generals, none failed to come to court.
proposals.reason: Chinese 柱國泰 includes the name Tai omitted in the literal English.

proposals.before: At the start of Sui's Kaihuang era, because Su Chuo had been famous in the former age, an edict was issued: "In olden days Emperor Gao of Han admired the righteousness of Wang Ling; Emperor Wu of Wei drew upon the spirit of Cao Zigan—former ages' eminent worthies were honored by later kings.
proposals.after: At the start of Sui's Kaihuang era, because Su Chuo had been famous in the former age, an edict was issued: "In olden days Emperor Gao of Han admired the righteousness of Wuji; Emperor Wu of Wei drew upon the spirit of Zigan—former ages' eminent worthies were honored by later kings.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 無忌 and 子幹; Wang Ling and the surname Cao are not in the source.

proposals.before: On the fourth day of the sixth month the Emperor offered morning rites at the Grand Temple; every officer was in his place.
proposals.after: On day dingsi of the sixth month the Emperor offered morning rites at the Grand Temple; every officer was in his place.
proposals.reason: 丁巳 is a sexagenary day, not necessarily "the fourth day" of the month.

proposals.before: Men like Yiyin the cook, Fuyue the prisoner, Gao Yao who "advanced in planting virtue," and Guan Zhong in humble obscurity are rarely celebrated in their own time;
proposals.after: Men like the cook, the convict laborer, the planter of virtue, and Guan Zhong in humble obscurity are rarely celebrated in their own time;
proposals.reason: Chinese 庖廚、胥靡、種德、微管 are allusive categories; only 微管 clearly abbreviates Guan Zhong, while Yiyin/Fuyue/Gao Yao are translator expansions.

proposals.before: Once Lü Wang was a butcher and fisherman, Baili Xi fed cattle, Ning Sheng played horn, and Guan Yiwu was defeated three times—at the time, who among ordinary men would have called them worthy?
proposals.after: In ancient times Lü Wang butchered and fished, Baili Xi fed cattle, Ning Qi beat time on an ox horn, and Guan Yiwu suffered three defeats. At the time, would ordinary observers have recognized their worth?
proposals.reason: s0164's 甯生 is the honorific 'Master Ning,' referring to Ning Qi, not a personal name 'Ning Sheng'; 扣角 describes beating time on an ox horn rather than playing a horn, and the revised final question follows 豈謂其賢 more naturally.

proposals.before: In old times Lü Wang butchered and fished, Baili Xi fed cattle, Ning Sheng beat horns, and Guan Yiwu was thrice defeated—at that time the drifting masses, how could they have called them worthy?
proposals.after: In old times Lü Wang butchered and fished, Baili Xi fed cattle, Master Ning beat time on an ox horn, and Guan Yiwu suffered three defeats. At that time, how could the common crowd have called them worthy?
proposals.reason: 甯生 literally uses 生 as an honorific, so 'Master Ning' is appropriate in the literal field; 扣角 is the ox-horn episode and the singular object should be retained.

decisions.reason: s0009 太祖未深知之 states that after more than a year Tai still did not know Su Chuo deeply; “before … truly knew his worth” turns the negation into eventual recognition of worth and misstates 未深知.

Wikisource Zhou Shu juan 23 reads 浸之以太和, confirming 乙 as a corruption of 以; the existing literal already follows that intended reading with “steep it in the Great Harmony,” so changing only “in” to “with” is stylistic.
s0236 contains only the fragment （五）; “[Since the Three Five]” invents a full temporal clause not present in this unit, while “Five” matches the supplied Chinese.

decisions.after: Since the Three, every age has had systems of taxation.
decisions.reason: s0237 has 三以來, so “since then” wrongly drops 三; Wikisource restores classical 三五以來 across the split with s0236’s （五）, but this unit’s Chinese alone supports “Since the Three,” not inventing “and Five” again here.
s0263 柱國泰 explicitly names Tai after the title 柱國; omitting that personal name is an error, and “Pillar-of-State Yuwen Tai” accurately identifies him in idiomatic English.
The same 柱國泰 requires the name in the literal field; “Pillar-of-State Tai” restores 泰 without adding matter absent from the Chinese.
s0379 has 漢高欽無忌之義，魏武挹子幹之風; Wang Ling and the surname Cao are not in the Chinese, and Wuji / Zigan correctly follow 無忌 and 子幹.

decisions.reason: s0270 dates the rites to 六月丁巳, a sexagenary day-name; rendering it as “the fourth day” invents an ordinal month-day the Chinese does not state.
s0406 lists 庖廚、胥靡、種德、微管 as allusive categories; naming Yiyin, Fuyue, and Gao Yao invents proper names not written in the unit, while keeping Guan Zhong for 微管 matches the clearest abbreviation.

decisions.reason: 甯生 is an honorific reference to Ning Qi, not a personal name 'Ning Sheng'; 扣角 is the familiar ox-horn episode and means beating time on the horn, while 豈謂其賢 asks whether observers would have recognized these men as worthy.

decisions.reason: 甯生 means Master Ning and identifies Ning Qi; 扣角 is singular and describes beating time on an ox horn, so the existing 'Ning Sheng beat horns' is inaccurate even as a literal rendering.
